source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
About one month after sowing in the germination bed, jackfruit seedlings can be transplanted into bags. The bags should be filled beforehand with a growing mix of one part compost soil, one part rice husk ash, and one part sand (a 1:1:1 mix). After transplanting, water immediately so the roots take hold in the new soil inside the bag.

The bagged seedlings should be kept under a shelter built from poles and woven palm-leaf thatch (as shown in the illustration), which shades the young plants while they establish.
